Setting L=K=Nr does not by itself equalize function evaluations: Algorithm 1 additionally performs DDIM simulations within rollouts. Appendix F asserts equal NFE without reporting actual counts or the simulation schedule. Table 23 also shows approximately 31% greater latency for hMCTS at N=81. Explicit accounting of gradient evaluations, rollout costs, and accuracy at matched wall-clock budgets is needed.

The necessity of the full training objective is not demonstrated across tasks. On Sudoku at N=321, Table 3 reports 39.06% for the full model with best-of-N, below 41.41% without MRNCL. Full VFScale with hMCTS reaches 42.97%, but the corresponding hMCTS experiment without MRNCL is missing. Consequently, the paper does not establish whether its novel loss improves the strongest Sudoku configuration; the proposed single-sample-versus-scalability explanation does not resolve this.

Comparisons are too narrow to establish competitiveness and novelty convincingly. Most experiments compare against one energy-diffusion baseline and the authors' own variants. The cited Monte Carlo Tree Diffusion work receives little substantive differentiation, and alternative search methods using the same learned energy are absent. Moreover, linear regression only narrowly exceeds the rank-based objective at N=81 in Table 12, without uncertainty estimates. Evaluation on two synthetic grid tasks also limits the broader reasoning claims.

Important implementation details remain unresolved. Algorithm 1 accumulates Q as a sum, while Equation 7 uses Q directly in UCB rather than its visit-normalized mean; the intended convention needs clarification. The MRNCL margin, entropy-estimator configuration, and differentiation through the sampling process are insufficiently specified. Training-step counts conflict between Tables 6–7 and Appendix B.5, while Table 7 lists 20 inner optimization steps and Appendix C says five are used.

Statistical reporting needs reconciliation. At N=81, the original Maze best-of-N baseline scores 0.1016 in Table 5 but 0.0609±0.0058 across ten seeds in Table 18, an unexplained discrepancy substantially larger than the reported standard deviation. The multi-seed analysis covers neither Sudoku nor the largest-budget headline result, leaving the smaller Sudoku improvements particularly uncertain.

Several mechanistic claims exceed the evidence. Local energy-versus-distance regression does not establish landscape smoothness or global navigability. Improved ranking and search success provide useful empirical support, but do not establish a generally reliable or near-perfect verifier; Table 19 even reports negative energy-quality correlations at the earliest denoising stages. These claims should be narrowed to the demonstrated settings.

strengths: The maze generalization results are substantial: training on sizes up to 6×6 yields 88.28% success on 15×15 mazes, versus 10.94% for the original model with best-of-N and 70.31% for VFScale training with best-of-N (Table 5).
Improving the model’s energy function for candidate ranking is a useful research direction. The combination of energy calibration and staged best-of-N/MCTS search has a plausible motivation.

The appendices contain meaningful additional evidence, including alternative ranking losses, corruption strategies, oracle comparisons, computational costs, and ten-seed maze experiments supporting the main performance gains.
weaknesses: The claimed equal-compute comparison is insufficiently substantiated. Setting L=K=Nr=N does not automatically equalize function evaluations when MCTS additionally performs DDIM simulations and terminal energy evaluations. Appendix F asserts equality without providing explicit accounting or the simulation schedule. Reported runtimes are useful, but the central efficiency claim needs auditable evaluation counts and accuracy-versus-runtime comparisons.

The benefit of the complete training objective is inconsistent across tasks. On Sudoku at N=321, KL-only training achieves 41.41% with best-of-N, exceeding the full objective’s 39.06% (Table 3). Full VFScale with hMCTS reaches 42.97%, but KL-only training with hMCTS is missing. Consequently, the contribution of MRNCL to the final Sudoku system remains unresolved. Sudoku also lacks the repeated-run evidence provided for Maze.

Novelty and competitive positioning need stronger support. Energy-based diffusion and KL regularization build directly on prior work, while the closely related Monte Carlo Tree Diffusion paper is cited without a detailed technical comparison or experimental baseline. Comparisons against alternative search strategies using the same learned energy would help establish the specific value of hMCTS.

Important implementation details are missing or inconsistent. The manuscript does not specify the MRNCL margin or sufficiently explain the entropy estimator and differentiation through sampling. Equation 7 uses Q in selection, whereas Algorithm 1 accumulates rewards into Q and normalizes only during final selection, leaving the intended UCB rule ambiguous. Table 7 specifies 20 inner optimization steps, while Appendix C selects five. The supplied PDF also contains no usable repository URL despite its reproducibility claims.

The evaluation protocol requires clarification. Many reported success rates appear quantized in increments of 1/128, although Appendix B lists 975 test mazes at size 15; the actual evaluated subset is unspecified. The original model’s N=81 result also changes from 10.16% in Table 5 to 6.09% ± 0.58% in Table 18 without explanation. Training versus inference seed variation and validation procedures are unclear.

Several interpretations exceed the evidence. Local energy ordering by distance to one reference solution does not establish global landscape smoothness or reliable discrete constraint satisfaction. Matching an oracle-guided success rate does not demonstrate a near-perfect verifier; Table 19 reports only moderate final-step rank correlation and negative correlations at high noise. The broader claims about intrinsic reasoning remain supported only by two structured grid tasks.
